label: rejected

evidence.V1: Tapered trunk with curving bare branches reads as a dead tree in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view reads as a radiating branch star
evidence.V2: Big trunk and medium branches exist, but small detail is thin: no real roots, no bark breaks or knots, only tiny twig spurs, so the hierarchy is partial
evidence.V3: Branches are uniform smooth horn-like tubes with pale pointed tips, reading more like antlers than gnarled wood; trunk is a straight faceted prism with a flat-cut top and a single skirt flare at the base
evidence.V4: Inconsistent: branches are soft smooth tubes while the trunk is hard-faceted and the root flare ends in thin razor-sharp skirt edges (close_roots_studio)
evidence.V5: Branch-to-trunk joints are not fused: in close_fork_studio/close_crown_studio the lower-left branch's butt end pokes out of the trunk as a dark hooked cap, and the right branch is a visible tube plugged into the side; hard light-tip colour bands on branches
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one bark brown in three values (dark stripes, mid, pale tips); ash/birch colourways keep the same structure
evidence.V7: 1320 tris vs tree target 2000 (ceiling 5000): at or under target
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material matches, but plugged-in separate tube branches contradict the kit's 'organic forms are fused smooth shells' rule and the razor root flare lacks the kit chamfer
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre

artifacts: Branch butt end protruding from trunk as a dark hooked cap (upper left fork)
Branches visibly plugged into trunk rather than fused (no blended collar)
top_fixes: Fuse branches into the trunk with blended collars and hide/remove the protruding branch butt ends
Replace the single skirt flare with 3-4 chunky root buttresses with chamfered edges
Add gnarl: bends/kinks in the trunk, a knot or broken-branch stub, and vary branch thickness so it reads as wood rather than antlers
